name: Indian Empire, c. 1909
source: Hand-drawn approximation after the Imperial Gazetteer of India, vol. 26, Atlas (1909), and Schwartzberg, A Historical Atlas of South Asia (1992), plate VIII.B.1 (p. 65), 'Territorial and administrative changes, 1857 to 1904'. One outline for British provinces and princely states together: the several hundred states (Hyderabad, Kashmir, Mysore, Rajputana, Central India and the rest) are inside it, not cut out. Includes Burma, a province of British India until 1937, and Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier up to the Durand Line. The Kashmir-Tibet line in Aksai Chin and the Assam hill frontier were undefined in 1909 and are drawn approximately. Excludes Aden, the Andaman and Nicobar and Laccadive islands, the French and Portuguese enclaves, Ceylon, Nepal and Bhutan. Good first issue: trace properly from the DSAL scans.
